page.layout: One column of verse in French with a heading "XV. Gal." and a Latin version headed "Lat." below it, then a horizontal rule and a second French heading "XVI. Gal." with its verse. Running head at top. Catchword "Car" at the lower right. No margin notes on this side.

main_text.head: XV. GAL.
main_text.p: PLUSTOST on pourra faire Le iour qui luit, N'auoir plus pour contraire L'obscure nuit, Et marier le feu Auecques l'onde: Que de conioindre Dieu Auec le Monde.
main_text.head: LAT.
main_text.p: MISCERI amico fœdere si simul Noctis tenebras videris aurea Cum luce Solis: si fluentes Ignibus hic socientur unda: Virtus relictis, credite, iurgiis Tunc blandienti cum vitio manus Pacata iunget fœderatas: Nec veteres memorabit iras.
main_text.head: XVI. GAL.
main_text.p: IE vi un iour le Monde combatant Contre Vertu, sa plus grande ennemie: Il la menasse, & elle le desfie, Il entre au camp,& elle l'y attend: Il marche,il vient,il s'approche,il luy tire: Mais tous ses coups ne peuvent avoir lieu:

page.notes: Faint show-through from the reverse page is visible in the right margin and was left out. The first word of each French stanza is set in small capitals; the first letter is a large initial. The Latin text is printed with a few ligatures and long-s-style letters, transcribed as plain letters. No doubtful readings.
